description.p: SuperV brings two Windows panels to Linux. Press Super+V to see the last 25 things you copied, text and images, and click one to paste it into the app you are using. Press Super+. for the emoji panel: type to search emoji, kaomoji and symbols, and the one you pick is typed where you were writing.

ul.li: Text and image history, newest first
Click or press Enter to paste into the app you were using
Pin items so they survive restarts; everything else clears on reboot, like Windows
Emoji panel: search by name, recently used first, skin tones, kaomoji ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ and symbols; your clipboard is put back afterwards
Turn each panel on or off in the settings; a panel that is off uses no memory and leaves its shortcut to your desktop
Choose your own shortcuts, a System, Light or Dark theme, and the text size
Move and resize the panel; SuperV remembers both
Works on GNOME, KDE Plasma, Cinnamon, MATE and Xfce, on Wayland and X11

description.p: Private by default: SuperV never connects to the internet, keeps your history only on your computer, and skips copies marked as passwords. It is one small C program (about 300 KB, emoji included). SuperV replaces SuperDot, the emoji panel that is now part of it.

screenshot.caption: Your clipboard history: text, code, links and images, in dark or light
Pin, delete or clear items from the ⋯ menu

description.p: The emoji panel joins SuperV: press Super+. for emoji, kaomoji and symbols, typed where you are writing. It replaces SuperDot and brings its settings along. Turn it off in the settings if you don't want it.
New tagline, "Clipboard for Linux", and packaging for the AUR, Fedora COPR and an Ubuntu/Mint PPA.
Screenshots in the app store: larger, landscape images that Ubuntu Software and GNOME Software can display.
Proper app-store listing: name, icon, screenshots, open-source licence, age rating and release notes in Ubuntu Software, GNOME Software and KDE Discover.
Packages for Fedora, openSUSE and Arch; SuperV restarts itself into a new version after an update; clicking outside always closes the panel; many fixes from a code review.
Browser image copies are saved as images; clearer settings menu with Reset; safer custom shortcuts.
